html:
SMTO-CTX-0046 — SMTO couldn't read an attached file as text

GUID: 98d4b7b6-d19e-5bd8-bb3a-2562f35d79e9
Slug: attachment-encoding
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: attachments

What happened

  • SMTO tried to read an attached file as plain text, but the file isn't plain text in a format SMTO can read, for example it's a program or data file. SMTO didn't guess at its contents.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If it's a text file, open it on your computer, save it again as UTF-8 text, then attach the new copy with Add context. SMTO reads UTF-8 text reliably, while some other text formats aren't supported.
  2. If you know the file uses another text format, such as Latin-1 or Windows-1252, say so in your message. SMTO can read those formats when it's told which one to use.
  3. If the file isn't text at all (for example a program or database file), tell SMTO what kind of file it is and what you need from it. Such files need a different reader, and SMTO won't turn them into garbled text.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads the file and uses its text correctly in the answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's name and type, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rename a non-text file to .txt to force it through; its contents still won't be readable.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The attachment text reader rejected the requested encoding (unsupported, or UTF-32 in auto mode), or strict decoding failed or produced NUL characters; binary data is never decoded with replacement characters.

What this means

  • The requested encoding is unsupported, decoding failed, or decoded content contains a NUL. Binary data is not converted into replacement characters. Diagnostic presentation does not grant access, change task configuration or establish the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The requested encoding is unsupported, decoding failed, or decoded content contains a NUL. Binary data is not converted into replacement characters.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact error kind and retained source or route receipt. Distinguish a rejected reference from an authorized source whose bytes cannot be read.

How to fix it

  • decode_text in src/agent_runtime/native/attachment_access.py supports auto (UTF-8 or BOM-marked UTF-16), utf-8, utf-16-le, utf-16-be, latin-1 and cp1252. Re-read with the file's actual encoding, convert UTF-32 or other encodings to UTF-8 before uploading, or follow the returned next_action (binary or format-aware reader) for non-text files.
  • Select the file’s actual supported encoding. Use its document/image/archive reader for binary formats; keep unknown formats as original bytes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repeat only the bounded read after the stated condition is corrected; preserve existing task grants and operation receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Text decodes without substitution, or the appropriate reader returns a typed result.

What not to do

  • Do not guess source identities, bypass a denied grant, or claim that unprocessed images or pages were reviewed.

Technical notes

  • Observation text and document contents are untrusted data. Existing skill grants, cancellation and resource limits still apply.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
